children: New Delhi, Oct. 15 -- Reliance Industries will become India's largest conglomerate by market capitalisation following the listing of Jio Platforms, Kotak Mahindra Bank founder Uday Kotak said on Thursday.

Set to open for subscription on October 21, the Jio IPO comes nearly two decades after Reliance's last major public offering and is poised to be India's largest-ever IPO, with an issue size of Rs.30,188 crore (based on upper price band).

Jio IPO is a testament to the development of the next generation of leadership in Reliance Industries, said Uday Kotak at the opening of the Jio Platforms IPO press conference. He also said Jio's years of perseverance had translated into market leadership in India's mobility and home broadband segments.

"From a data-scarce nation of less than 4 crore 4G customers to a data-abundant nation of 100 crore 4G and 5G customers happened over the last 10 years," said Kotak while underlining that "Jio is the only player globally with proprietary end-to-end digital connectivity stack."

"I remember 2016, and many of the other players were saying, 'What are Reliance Group going to do?' But when they came, they came with a bang. They transformed the concept of how mobile connectivity and digital in India would be in the years to come. It transformed the lives of every individual, who got lower prices for the service, and democratised internet connectivity in the country," he added.

"We expect a USD 1.4-trillion digital economy by FY31; we will take a huge market share of this," Akash Ambani, managing director of Jio Platforms, said on Thursday, outlining the company's growth strategy across mobile connectivity, home broadband and enterprise services.

Akash Ambani also outlined Jio's strategy built around technology, digital connectivity and infrastructure, supported by three growth engines - mobility, home broadband, and enterprise and international services. Jio had 533.3 million customers as of June 30, 2026, including 285 million 5G users, making it the largest 5G customer base outside China, Akash Ambani highlighted. He also pointed out that Jio carries over 60 per cent of India's data traffic.

Jio Platforms, the telecom and digital services arm of Reliance Industries, will open its initial public offering on October 21, according to its red herring prospectus. It will be the listing of India's largest mobile carrier by subscribers.

Jio Platforms IPO is a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares with a face value of Rs.10 each, with no offer-for-sale component. Jio IPO upper price band is fixed at Rs.1,065 to Rs.1,119 per share. The IPO will close on Friday, October 23, with anchor bidding scheduled for Monday, October 19.
Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) owns 66.43% of Jio Platforms.
